newsitem.title: USA: Photographer gets life in prison for model's murder.
newsitem.headline: Photographer gets life in prison for model's murder.

text.p: A freelance photographer was sentenced on Monday to life in prison without the possibility of parole for the murder of model Linda Sobek.
Charles Rathbun, 38, was convicted last month of murdering Sobek, a former Los Angeles Raiders football team cheerleader he had hired for a photo shoot.
Superior Court Judge Donald Pitts, who handed down the sentence, called him a monster who subjected Sobek to "a death of unspeakable horror and brutality."

Rathbun buried Sobek's body last year in a shallow grave in the Angeles National Forest but later led police to the site after he became a focus of suspicion. At his trial he maintained Sobek's death had been an accident, initially claiming to have struck her while practicing stunts in a sport utility vehicle he was assigned to photograph.

After an autopsy showed Sobek had been suffocated, Rathbun changed his story and claimed he had accidentally asphyxiated her while they were having consensual sex -- a story the prosecution challenged.
